title: Identification and an Information Bound for Latent Stages with an Absorbing Failure State: A Neural Hidden Markov Model of Young Firms
content: Latent stage models for short panels with an absorbing outcome raise two information-theoretic questions: when can the outcome identify the stages, and how much can it tell about them? We study a neural hidden Markov model with hurdle Student-t emissions, context-dependent transitions and an absorbing failure state whose exit status enters the likelihood. We show that two observations followed by an observed exit identify stages, emission laws, transitions and hazards when hazards differ across stages, and that the mutual information between the last stage and the exit status is bounded by ρ log(1 + D), where ρ is the share of observed exits and D the χ² contrast of the hazards; the same quantity bounds the Fisher information the exit adds and the emission fit it can trade away. The number of stages is selected by the integrated completed likelihood, whose classification-entropy penalty is combined with bootstrap stability and out-of-fold prediction. On 8304 Italian innovative start-ups three stages—dormant, operating and distress—are selected; the exit carries 0.002 nats per firm (3% of its entropy), so the stages are identified by the accounts and failure contributes stage-specific, age-dependent hazards. Simulations confirm that the exit view helps only when the bound is large.
